en: The Apadāna of the Elder Rahosaññaka Sobhita Chapter 5 I was a merchant’s son in the city of Benares, And I gave a single mango fruit to the Buddha Vipassī. Because of that root of merit, I have been reborn in heaven; For twenty thousand aeons, I dwelt in the realm of the gods. When the world was empty of Buddhas, I became a wheel-turning monarch; In every birth, I possessed the power of recollection. Having passed away from there, I was born in the human world; I was a king named Mahāsena, lord of the earth. I ruled over the four great continents together with their islands; I was a righteous king, a conqueror of all quarters. I gave alms to the Saṅgha of monks led by the Buddha Kassapa; I served them with food and drink, robes, and bedding. Through that kamma, I have attained this supreme state; I am now the Elder Rahosaññaka, dwelling in the forest. I have lived for eighty-four thousand years; My life-span is now at its end, and I shall pass away. Having abandoned this human body, I shall go to the Brahma-world; There I shall dwell for sixty-four thousand aeons. From there, passing away, I shall go to the Tusita realm; There I shall dwell for thirty-two thousand aeons. From there, passing away, I shall go to Nimmānarati; There I shall dwell for sixteen thousand aeons. From there, passing away, I shall go to Paranimmitavasavatti; There I shall dwell for eight thousand aeons. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Thirty-Three; There I shall dwell for four thousand aeons. From there, passing away, I shall go to the Yāma realm; There I shall dwell for two thousand aeons. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Four Great Kings; There I shall dwell for one thousand aeons. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Cātumahārājika; There I shall dwell for five hundred aeons. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Tāvatiṃsa; There I shall dwell for two hundred and fifty aeons. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Yāma; There I shall dwell for one hundred and twenty-five aeons. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Tusita; There I shall dwell for sixty-two and a half aeons. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Nimmānarati; There I shall dwell for thirty-one and a quarter aeons. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Paranimmitavasavatti; There I shall dwell for fifteen and a quarter aeons. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Cātumahārājika; There I shall dwell for seven and a half aeons. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Tāvatiṃsa; There I shall dwell for three and three-quarter aeons. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Yāma; There I shall dwell for one and three-quarter aeons. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Tusita; There I shall dwell for six months and twelve and a half days. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Nimmānarati; There I shall dwell for three months and six days. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Paranimmitavasavatti; There I shall dwell for one month and three days. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Cātumahārājika; There I shall dwell for fifteen days. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Tāvatiṃsa; There I shall dwell for seven and a half days. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Yāma; There I shall dwell for three and three-quarter days. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Tusita; There I shall dwell for one day and twelve hours. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Nimmānarati; There I shall dwell for six hours. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Paranimmitavasavatti; There I shall dwell for three hours. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Cātumahārājika; There I shall dwell for one hour and a half. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Tāvatiṃsa; There I shall dwell for three-quarters of an hour. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Yāma; There I shall dwell for one hour. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Tusita; There I shall dwell for thirty minutes. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Nimmānarati; There I shall dwell for fifteen minutes. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Paranimmitavasavatti; There I shall dwell for seven and a half minutes. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Cātumahārājika; There I shall dwell for three and three-quarter minutes. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Tāvatiṃsa; There I shall dwell for one minute and thirty seconds. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Yāma; There I shall dwell for thirty seconds. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Tusita; There I shall dwell for twelve seconds. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Nimmānarati; There I shall dwell for six seconds. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Paranimmitavasavatti; There I shall dwell for three seconds. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Cātumahārājika; There I shall dwell for one and a half seconds. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Tāvatiṃsa; There I shall dwell for three-quarters of a second. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Yāma; There I shall dwell for one second. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Tusita; There I shall dwell for thirty milliseconds.

From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Nimmānarati; There I shall dwell for fifteen milliseconds. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Paranimmitavasavatti; There I shall dwell for seven and a half milliseconds. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Cātumahārājika; There I shall dwell for three and three-quarter milliseconds. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Tāvatiṃsa; There I shall dwell for one millisecond and thirty microseconds. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Yāma; There I shall dwell for thirty microseconds. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Tusita; There I shall dwell for twelve microseconds. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Nimmānarati; There I shall dwell for six microseconds. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Paranimmitavasavatti; There I shall dwell for three microseconds. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Cātumahārājika; There I shall dwell for one and a half microseconds. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Tāvatiṃsa; There I shall dwell for three-quarters of a microsecond. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Yāma; There I shall dwell for one microsecond. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Tusita; There I shall dwell for thirty nanoseconds. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Nimmānarati; There I shall dwell for fifteen nanoseconds. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Paranimmitavasavatti; There I shall dwell for seven and a half nanoseconds. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of the Cātumahārājika; There I shall dwell for three and three-quarter nanoseconds. From there, passing away, I shall go to the realm of
"Not far from the Himālaya is a mountain named Vasabha;
at the foot of that mountain,"
A hermitage was built there.
At that time, as a brahmin, I taught three thousand students.
Having gathered those disciples together,
I sat down to one side.
Having sat down to one side, I...
A brahmin who had mastered the mantras,
seeking the Buddha-veda,
clarified his mind in wisdom.
Having inspired confidence there in my mind,
I sat down upon a bed of leaves;
having folded my legs crosswise in the full lotus posture, I remained.
I passed away there;
thirty-one eons ago,
that was when I attained perception.
I do not know a state of woe;
this is the fruit of my perception through knowledge.
In the twenty-seventh aeon,
There was a king named Siridhara;
endowed with the seven treasures,
he was a wheel-turning monarch of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Rahosaññaka spoke these verses.
This is the fifth legend of the elder Rahosaññaka.
